new_entities.name: Cesarean birth
new_entities.description: Birth by cesarean section rather than vaginal delivery.

new_entities.name: Long-term childhood atopy
new_entities.description: Later childhood atopic disease including asthma, eczema, allergic rhinitis, food allergy, or allergic sensitization.

edges.effect_quant: A 2018 meta-analysis found that cesarean delivery was associated with higher childhood asthma risk, and older meta-analytic and population data also suggest modest increases across broader atopic outcomes, although effect sizes are generally small.
edges.population: children followed after cesarean versus vaginal birth
edges.mechanism: Cesarean birth may alter early microbial colonization and immune education, contributing to later allergic sensitization and atopic disease risk.
edges.summary: Cesarean birth is associated with a modestly higher long-term risk of childhood atopic outcomes overall, especially asthma and allergic sensitization.
edges.caveats: Observed effects are modest and may partly reflect residual confounding by indication or maternal and perinatal factors. Associations vary across allergic outcomes and study settings.

evidence.citation: Bager P et al 2008 Clin Exp Allergy
evidence.notes: Caesarean delivery and risk of atopy and allergic disease: meta-analyses.

evidence.notes: Caesarean delivery, childhood asthma, and effect modification by sex: An observational study and meta-analysis.
